text:
## Common Mistakes (Don't Make These!)  
❌ **Mistake 1:** Ignoring a potential match and processing transaction anyway
✅ **Correct:** Escalate to Compliance, do not process  
❌ **Mistake 2:** Telling customer "We're checking if you're on a sanctions list"
✅ **Correct:** Do not disclose screening to customer (tipping-off is illegal)  
❌ **Mistake 3:** Closing account without investigation
✅ **Correct:** Report suspicious activity to Compliance first  
❌ **Mistake 4:** Only screening at account opening
✅ **Correct:** Screen continuously throughout customer relationship  
---
name: Chunk 13/61

raw_entities.name: Processing Transaction Despite Potential Match
raw_entities.description: A critical operational error where staff proceed with transaction processing when a potential sanctions or PEP list match has been identified. This represents a failure to escalate and investigate before execution, creating direct compliance and legal risk.
context: Mistake 1: Ignoring a potential match and processing transaction anyway
Correct: Escalate to Compliance, do not process

raw_entities.name: Disclosing Sanctions Screening to Customer
raw_entities.description: A prohibited disclosure where staff inform a customer that they are being checked against sanctions or PEP lists. This constitutes tipping-off, which is illegal under AML regulations and alerts subjects to investigation.
context: Mistake 2: Telling customer 'We're checking if you're on a sanctions list'
Correct: Do not disclose screening to customer (tipping-off is illegal)

raw_entities.name: Account Closure Without Prior Investigation
raw_entities.description: A procedural failure where an account is closed in response to suspicious activity without first reporting to Compliance and conducting investigation. This bypasses mandatory SAR obligations and creates audit and regulatory exposure.
context: Mistake 3: Closing account without investigation
Correct: Report suspicious activity to Compliance first

raw_entities.name: One-Time Screening at Account Opening Only
raw_entities.description: A compliance gap where AML screening is performed only at account opening and not repeated throughout the customer relationship. This fails to detect changes in customer risk profile, sanctions list additions, or adverse media developments over time.
context: Mistake 4: Only screening at account opening
Correct: Screen continuously throughout customer relationship

raw_entities.name: Escalation to Compliance on Potential Match
raw_entities.description: Staff must escalate any potential sanctions or PEP list match to Compliance immediately and must not process the transaction pending investigation. This is a mandatory action that takes precedence over transaction processing.
context: Escalate to Compliance, do not process

raw_entities.name: Prohibition on Tipping-Off During Screening
raw_entities.description: Staff must not disclose to customers that they are being screened against sanctions or PEP lists. Tipping-off is illegal under AML law and alerts subjects to investigation, compromising compliance effectiveness.
context: Do not disclose screening to customer (tipping-off is illegal)

raw_entities.name: Mandatory Compliance Reporting Before Account Closure
raw_entities.description: Staff must report suspicious activity to Compliance and conduct investigation before closing an account. Account closure decisions must follow, not precede, compliance review and SAR filing where required.
context: Report suspicious activity to Compliance first

raw_entities.name: Continuous AML Screening Throughout Customer Relationship
raw_entities.description: Staff must perform AML screening not only at account opening but continuously throughout the entire customer relationship. This ongoing monitoring detects changes in risk profile, new sanctions list entries, and adverse media developments.
context: Screen continuously throughout customer relationship
